thread:
alice.dev: Running into an SDK vs REST parity issue: REST accepts `stop_sequences` as an array but Go SDK only accepts a string. Sampleapp's multi-stop test is failing.
bob: can you share the REST payload and the SDK call?
alice.dev: REST:
```
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"small-1","prompt":"foo","stop_sequences":["\n","###","END"]}'
# => 200, stops honored
```
Go SDK (current):
```go
client.Generate(ctx, GenerateParams{
  Model: "small-1",
  Prompt: "foo",
  StopSequences: "\n,###,END",
})
// result: only first stop matched (newline), others ignored
```
charlie: looks like the Go SDK serializer joins slices into a comma string. Should send JSON array to REST.
alice.dev: exactly. The conversion lives in pkg/serialize/params.go: `if v, ok := v.([]string); ok { return strings.Join(v, ",") }` which is wrong for endpoints expecting arrays.
ci-bot: failing test: sampleapp/tests/e2e/test_multi_stop.py::test_multiple_stop_sequences - 1 failed. Logs: ci://artifacts/2087654300/stop_test.log
bob: Proposed fix: change serializer to preserve arrays and send as JSON arrays for body parameters. Add per-endpoint mapping so we don't accidentally change query param behavior where comma-join is expected.
charlie: also update Go SDK docs to show StopSequences as []string and update other SDKs if they have same pattern (ruby maybe). Add a quick integration test in sampleapp that posts an explicit REST payload and asserts sdk.Generate returns equivalent behavior.
alice.dev: opening PR with fix + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/211 - changes serialize logic, adds e2e test, and a note in the changelog.
bob: nice. Also add a migration note in SDK migration guide: "StopSequences transition: SDKs now preserve arrays and pass as JSON arrays to REST; if you were passing comma-separated strings, update call sites."
charlie: follow-up: scan for other multi-valued params (allowed_formats, response_format, stop_sequences, candidate_labels) to ensure consistent treatment across SDKs. I filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/174 (multi-valued-param-parity-scan).
alice.dev: thanks — merging once CI green. Will update the sampleapp quickstart snippet and onboarding checklist to include a test for stop sequences.
